thread:
elaine_support: customer reports tool call returning 400 \"invalid JSON\" when passing file path in args. here's the payload they sent and the error they got.

elaine_support: ```json
{
  \"action\": \"upload\",
  \"path\": \"C:\\Users\\bob\\Documents\\report.pdf\",
  \"metadata\": {
    \"source\": \"excel paste\",
  },
}
```

elaine_support: response from our API: `{\"error\":\"tool_call_failed\",\"message\":\"Failed to parse tool args: invalid JSON\"}`

tyler_eng: can you paste the raw HTTP request (headers + body) they sent? suspect content-type or extra characters.

elaine_support: they gave this curl after we asked for raw:```bash
curl -X POST \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/call_tool\" \\
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-customer\" \\
  -H \"Content-Type: text/plain\" \\
  -d '{\"action\":\"upload\",\"path\":\"C:\\Users\\bob\\Documents\\report.pdf\", \"metadata\": {\"source\": \"excel paste\", }, }'
```

sophie_support: ah, Content-Type is text/plain and body includes trailing commas + backslashes. JSON parser will choke on both.

tyler_eng: yep — two problems: trailing commas after \"source\" object and at the top-level, plus backslashes must be escaped in JSON string (they are here but with text/plain the client might have munged them). if client pasted from Windows, sometimes single backslashes get interpreted by shell or by some middle proxy. we should tell them to use application/json and to escape or use forward slashes.

elaine_support: customer says they just pasted from Excel UI into a web form (our SDK form). they didn't realize it inserted smart quotes earlier. here's what they claimed the UI sent (they pasted visually):```json
{\"action\":\"upload\",\"path\":\"C:\\Users\\bob\\Documents\\report.pdf\", \"metadata\": {\"source\": \"excel paste\", }, }
```

tyler_eng: ok. we should reproduce. nate_repro — can you try with a minimal repro using the SDK to see exact parser error we return? put it in eng-oncall if it's a parser bug.

deploy-bot: Automatically moving thread to #eng-oncall for triage.

nate_repro: repro'd locally. our parser returns a generic \"invalid JSON\" from the function-calling layer. stack shows it fails at JSON.parse due to trailing comma token. backslashes aren't the root cause in my run.

nate_repro: quick notes:
- With Content-Type: application/json and body fixed (no trailing commas) the call succeeds.
- With trailing commas we return 400 but the message doesn't indicate location (line/col).

nate_repro: patch suggestion: improve error to include snippet and pointer like \"unexpected token ',' at line X col Y\" so support/customer can fix. filing parser ticket.

tyler_eng: good. mitigation for customer: 1) set Content-Type: application/json, 2) remove trailing commas, 3) double escape backslashes or use forward slashes, 4) advise them to JSON.stringify() in browser before send. share this example curl they can copy:```bash
curl -X POST \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/call_tool\" \\
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-customer\" \\
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\
  -d '{\"action\":\"upload\",\"path\":\"C:\\\\Users\\\\bob\\\\Documents\\\\report.pdf\",\"metadata\": {\"source\": \"excel paste\"}}'
```

elaine_support: also to note: if they submit via form field that sends as text/plain our middle tier doesn't always re-encode — we should add a validation check to return a clearer 400 advising correct content-type. adding RFC-compliant error message to support template.

nate_repro: ticket created: PARSER-4021 — improve error details + validate content-type on entry path. I attached unit repro and a small fix for clearer error strings.

elaine_support: thanks team. i'll send the customer the curl example and ask them to retry. will update here when they confirm. :thumbsup:
